title: Streamline synthetic load generator and metrics plumbing for perf regression reliability
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Our current synthetic load harness (loadgen) is brittle, mixes concerns (scenario generation, orchestration, metrics enrichment) and runs as a collection of heterogeneous scripts. This causes flaky perf regressions, hard-to-reproduce runs in CI, and duplicated logic across eval/pipeline codepaths.

Goal: Refactor the harness into clear, testable components: a lightweight runner (stateless, low overhead), a scenario library (versioned YAML/JSON fixtures), and a metrics enrichment/ingestion pipeline that writes consistent schema to Prometheus/Influx and a canonical benchmark artifact (NDJSON). Also upgrade runtime dependencies to remove known contention and memory leaks. Deliverables: modular runner (Go), scenario versioning + CI smoke, metrics adapter, migration guide, and perf regression baseline updates.
acceptance_criteria: New runner replaces >90% of current python-based loadgen use cases and is exercised by unit tests
CI job `perf/smoke` runs deterministic scenarios in <10m and passes stability checks (stddev < 5% for TPS across 5 runs)
Metrics emitted conform to schema v2 and dashboards ingest without transformation
Benchmark artifacts (NDJSON) produced for each run and stored in s3 path s3://redwood-perf/benchmarks/2026/, accessible from perf-console
Upgrade PRs merged for critical dependencies (locust->k6 adapter removed, protobuf bumped, http client lib patched) with no regressions in runtime tests
technical_notes: Proposed runner implementation: Go binary using fasthttp + goroutines to keep client overhead low; minimal dependencies, single static binary for CI and dedicated nodes
Scenario library: move from ad-hoc JS files to compressed YAML fixtures with template variables and canonical metadata (seed, token lengths, model variant)
Metrics plumbing: introduce an adapter that emits three outputs: Prometheus metrics, NDJSON artifact for traceability, and a condensed summary (JSON) for quick comparisons in the perf console
CI integration: add `perf/smoke` pipeline using ephemeral dedicated infra (preemptible GPUs) and gating for PRs touching runtime or eval code
Dependency upgrades: bump github.com/golang/protobuf -> google.golang.org/protobuf; remove transitive `github.com/legacy/retry` known to leak goroutines; vendor locked for stable CI runs
comments: 2026-02-20 Priya Kapoor: Triage notes — assigned to Ethan. Identified three problem areas: high-overhead python runner, inconsistent metric schemas, flaky CI smoke tests. Linked initial spike doc.

2026-02-24 Ethan Marshall: Spike complete — built PoC Go runner (repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/loadgen/pull/4321). Early results: runner uses ~40% CPU vs python runner at same RPS; memory is stable across 10k concurrent connections.

2026-03-02 QA: Ran 5 baseline runs against staging: stddev TPS = 12%, 99p latency variance high. Hypothesis: client-side GC and asyncio backpressure causing jitter. Proceed with Go runner and metrics unification.

2026-03-05 Design review: Reviewed schema v2 for metrics; agreed on field names, required tags (scenario_id, run_id, model_tag, region). Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PERF/Load+Harness+Metrics+Schema

2026-03-09 Dev update: Implemented NDJSON artifact writer + S3 uploader (s3://redwood-perf/benchmarks/2026/ENG-26789/). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/loadgen/pull/4339 — awaiting infra creds review

2026-03-12 Perf results: Migrated one canonical scenario to Go runner. Throughput +18% median, 99p latency reduced by 9% and variance across runs dropped to 4.3%. Draft migration plan posted in ticket. Next: complete CI integration and wrap up dependency bump PRs.
